key_insight: A structured ten-step LLM-assisted workflow can support machine-checked verification of complex algorithms in Dafny while shifting human effort toward supervision and specification review.
engineering_relevance: Combining LLM-generated proof work with testing, verifier feedback, and performance profiling offers a practical route to verifying sophisticated scientific software.
method: Formalize algorithms and develop contracts and invariants.
Validate invariants empirically and iteratively construct proofs using Dafny feedback.
Profile verification bottlenecks and optimize proofs under human oversight.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluated the workflow on 37 algorithms from graph theory and labelled transition systems, including the Hopcroft–Tarjan triconnectivity test, with many verifications completed within hours to a few days.
watch_item: Human review remains essential: machine-checked proofs establish the specified properties, not whether the specifications capture every intended requirement.
